answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a ember as the anchor of the cost. A nectar stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a canyon...
